title: Paper nomogram or computer-assisted warfarin dosing in a three-site anticoagulation clinic: design deferred until the INR records are profiled
subtitle: Design not yet settled: records comparison or randomised comparison
statement: Two warfarin dosing approaches run side by side in one anticoagulation clinic: a paper nomogram at the main site and a computer-assisted dosing tool at two satellite clinics since October 2025. The medical director wants to standardise by next spring, but the approaches have never been compared, the sites differ in case mix, and it is not known whether the INR records are complete enough to calculate time in therapeutic range. The design question is open: a comparison of existing records may be biased or impossible, and a randomised comparison of new referrals would be slow.
whoAffected: About 1,150 adults on warfarin, many older and on interacting medicines, the clinic pharmacists at three sites, and the anticoagulation committee that must approve any change.
whatHurts: Time outside the therapeutic range raises the risk of bleeding and of stroke or valve thrombosis; standardising on the wrong approach, or on the right one for the wrong reasons, would affect every patient in the clinic.
currentPractice: Main site: dose adjusted from the latest INR with a paper nomogram. Satellites: weekly dose suggested by the dosing tool from the last three INRs and confirmed by the pharmacist. Home test results are entered by clerical staff with unrecorded delay.
whyNow: Standardisation is planned for next spring, and the satellite pharmacists' confidence in the software has not been tested against the clinic's own data.
constraints: No research funding. Pharmacist time for data work is limited to about four hours a week. Patient-identifiable clinic records may not leave the hospital network. Any change to dosing practice needs approval from the anticoagulation committee.
patientCenteredGoal: Every patient spends as much time as possible in the safe INR range with the fewest dose changes and clinic contacts, whichever approach the clinic keeps.
summary: Problem framed; the design family is left unresolved because both candidate designs depend on data whose completeness is unknown.
